intro: This is Race Control: an AI referee and game master for Twitch, where a solo streamer plays against their own chat.
dare: The streamer types dare. The Game Master, a live Codex call, writes a fresh dare for this game in a few seconds.
approve: Nothing goes live without the streamer. They approve it, or reroll for a new one.
vote: Now chat votes on the loadout: a number, the option's first word, or pick. Fans also predict whether the streamer will make it.
locked: The vote locks, and from here nobody types kills.
watcher: The Watcher reads the kill counter straight from the game HUD through OBS, using on-device text recognition, and books every kill in the Ledger.
won: Target reached: dare won. Fans who called it score a point, all derived by replaying the Ledger.
rule: Now the streamer changes the rules, in plain English: wrong calls lose a point.
audit: The Rules Compiler, one Codex model, writes the scoring code. The Auditor, a second model, writes its own without seeing the first.
adopt: They must agree on every case: {cases} out of {cases}. The streamer previews the new standings, then adopts the rule.
replay: The whole stream is re-scored. Fans who guessed wildly drop, and careful fans climb.
outro: Race Control was built in a single Codex thread, and Codex runs three of its agents live. Streamer versus chat, refereed by agents.
watcher+: Each kill needs two matching reads, and impossible jumps are ignored, so one glitchy frame can't win a dare.
